recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

recEDO3WWWhzVkwgI.Bio: Matt Presti is a metascientist, musician, and host of The Exploration of Consciousness (TEC) podcast, known for his long-running study of the science and philosophy of Walter Russell. His work centers on light, universal law, and cosmology, and on InnerVerse he has explored Russell's teachings alongside critiques of mainstream physics.
recEDO3WWWhzVkwgI.Name: Matt Presti

fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Matt Presti is the current President of the University of Science & Philosophy, an organization dedicated to sharing the works of Walter and Lao Russell, and preserving their artistic legacy. In this episode we talk about the Walter Russell Museum that Matt helped create, the nature of the Higher Self, Imagination, balancing our inner polarities, the shadow, and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Demons as Divided Pieces of the Self", "body": "Chance opens the members' hour by reading demon as a divided, compartmentalized one: a shard of the self walled off by trauma, cut from source and left to feed on others. Matt answers with the Russells, who pointed straight at mankind and called demons and devils figments of man's imagination, and with Jung's view of the shadow as something that keeps demanding attention until it is faced. Because nature holds no evil, only imbalances righting themselves, Matt argues that evil is born of free will and inner division, and that a person divided inside will act out that division on the world."}, {"title": "Arresting the Thought and Finding the Real Self", "body": "Matt describes borrowing Eckhart Tolle's phrase about arresting your thoughts and turning it into a daily practice: stop the critical voice, examine it, and notice that whatever is doing the examining is the real self. He frames this through Plato's cave, with the ego watching shadows and the soul as the light behind it, the still small voice that grows audible as the mind quiets. Chance builds on it with the spiritual warrior as the watcher on the wall, then plays with language, setting thinking as a thin king against waking as the way of the king, and inward directed thought against automatic, stimulus driven thinking."}, {"title": "Mass Movements and the Death Half of the Wave", "body": "Drawing on Walter Russell's white light of mind, which Matt pictures as an inverted galaxy he calls a selfie of God, the two contrast the mastery of thought with what Matt calls its de-mastery. In his reading, the unrest of 2020 is an externalized, outward living expression that belongs to the death half of the wave of creation, marked by destruction, graffiti and fear rather than construction and inspiration, and the two read the mask as a symbol of the mind turned outward. Matt links the moment to the flu and revolution of 1918, and Chance adds a 52-year cycle that also runs through 1968."}, {"title": "The Electric Body, Tuning Forks and Calories", "body": "Chance raises the book The Invisible Rainbow and the theory that illness is electrical, a matter of stuck and stagnant polarity in a person's field rather than a material cause with a name. He walks through biofield tuning as he understands it from Eileen Day McKusick's books, with tuning forks combing stuck energy back toward the body's central column. Matt relates it to Rife's frequency work, then argues the body is no combustion engine: calories are not burned, food replaces dying cells, and real power comes from mind, citing his own nine-day fast in 2009 and Walter Russell living five lives in one."}, {"title": "Rhythm, Silence and Dividing the Stillness", "body": "Chance turns to music and counterculture, asking how frequency and fame can be used to manipulate audiences on the festival circuit, and how to sense what music does to you. Matt points listeners to Lenon Honor on the roots of hip hop, then explains why the Russells disliked heavily syncopated music: it divides the universal one, two of the heartbeat until the silence between notes disappears. He calls sobriety the strongest drug he has known, and Chance links returning to stillness with backing out of time and Saturn. Matt closes on creation as dividing silence and stillness with the will, from a song to a chicken coop."}]
